en: The Analysis of the Bhikkhunī Rules,

2.7 The Chapter on Settling (Samathavāra) For a lustful bhikkhunī who consents to bodily contact with a lustful person, by how many of the seven principles for settling disputes are her offenses settled?
For a lustful bhikkhunī who consents to bodily contact with a lustful person, her offenses are settled by three of the seven principles for settling disputes.
It may be settled by both *sammukhāvinaya* and *paṭiññātakaraṇa*; it may be settled by both *sammukhāvinaya* and *tiṇavatthāraka* ...
[and so on]. How many of the seven principles for settling disputes settle the offenses of one who eats having requested curd?
The offenses of one who eats having requested curd are settled by three of the seven principles for settling disputes.
It may be by means of both resolution face-to-face and acting according to what is admitted; it may be by means of both resolution face-to-face and covering over as with grass.
The seventh section on the settlement of disputes is finished.
